source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 761 Ch. 511 — Special Permits for Excess Size and Weight; Iowa Code 321E.14 (fees)
verify_reasons: Iowa publishes no fixed numeric width/height/length superload threshold in 761 Ch. 511; the only official structural-review trigger is combined gross > 100,000 lbs on a single-trip permit (discretionary undue-damage review) — dimensional superload fields are null by design.

General single-semitrailer length limit is set by Iowa Code 321.457 and is not numerically restated in Ch. 511 (53' used as the cross-referenced value); a 2025 single-trip overweight ton fee (HF 979) may apply and was not visible in the 321E.14 text read — confirm current single-trip overweight cost with Iowa DOT.

superload_thresholds.note: Iowa 761 Ch. 511 publishes no fixed dimensional superload numbers — single-trip width/height/length are limited to the physical clearances of the roadway (761-511.13(1)); loads over 16' high must contact utility owners. The only numeric engineering gate: a single-trip permit for combined gross over 100,000 lbs is issued only if the issuing authority determines it will not cause undue damage to the road (761-511.17(4)b).

width.note: 4-lane: rear escort (amber strobe on power unit + rear may substitute); 2-lane: front escort (761-511.20(2))

height.note: front escort with a height pole; escort must measure all vertical clearances (761-511.20(1)j)

length.note: rear escort over 120' overall (both 4-lane and 2-lane); 85'-120' requires flags + amber lights only

single_trip.fee_formula: Single-trip permit = $35 (Iowa Code 321E.14(1)e). Add-ons: single-trip registration fee $4 per ton over 40 tons (761-511.5(5)); buildings 5 cents/ton per mile over registered weight; duplicate permit $2. Escort service fee up to $250/day per escort (321E.14(3)). A 2025 single-trip overweight ton fee (HF 979) may also apply — confirm with Iowa DOT.
single_trip.note: Special/emergency oversize permit for divisible loads = $35. Multitrip permits valid <=60 days.

annual.note: Annual $50; annual all-systems oversize $160; annual all-systems overweight $500; multitrip $400; special alt-energy multitrip $600; raw forest products annual $175; fluid milk annual $400.

movement_restrictions: Daylight movement only: one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset (761-511.3(3))
Move only when roads are clear of ice/snow and visibility is at least one-quarter mile (761-511.3(2))

Continuous (including night) travel allowed only if width <=12', height <=14'6", length <=100', legal axle weights, roadway >=22'/lanes >=11', with red rear lamps and amber front-corner lamps (761-511.3(5))
No movement on Memorial Day, Independence Day, or Labor Day, none after 12 noon the day before, and none during those holiday weekends (761-511.3(4))
Compacted-rubbish vehicles exempt — allowed day/night, 7 days including holidays
notes: Legal width 8'6", height 13'6", gross 80,000 lbs. Ch. 511 states a 75' overall-combination statutory limit; the general single-semitrailer length is set by Iowa Code 321.457 (53' cross-referenced).

Axle limits (761-511.17): single 20,000 lbs; permitted tandem up to 46,000 lbs (max 24,000/axle, >=4 tires each); tridem/quad higher with tire spec; annual OS/OW and raw-forest max 156,000 lbs total; single-trip over 100,000 lbs gross is discretionary.

Escort matrix (761-511.20(2)) and fees (Iowa Code 321E.14) sourced verbatim from Iowa Administrative Code / Iowa Code; iowadot.gov brochure pages were 403-blocked so the DOT's own codified rules were used instead. No numeric police-escort threshold — an on-duty peace officer is contacted as needed for traffic control.
State-level rules only — county/city permits, bridge-specific engineering and low-clearance routing are out of scope.
